'''Silvia Giordani''' (born 1973) is an Italian chemist who is Professor of Nanomaterials at [[Dublin City University]]. Her research considers carbon-based functional materials for biotechnology. She was awarded a [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science]] fellowship in 2012.

== Early life and education ==
Giordani was born in [[Bergamo]] in [[Italy]].<ref name="Barry">{{Cite web|last=Barry|first=Aoife|title=Trinity scientist wins £15k award - a boost as funding shrinks|url=https://www.thejournal.ie/science-loreal-award-trinity-silvia-giordani-508644-Jul2012/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=TheJournal.ie|date=8 July 2012 |language=en}}</ref> She was an undergraduate student at the [[University of Milan]], where she completed a Laura in pharmaceutical chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|last=PORCIANI|first=FRANCA|title=Silvia Giordani, cervello in fuga: "Vorrei tornare, ma non posso"|url=http://bergamo.corriere.it/bergamo/notizie/cronaca/12_maggio_28/cervelli-silvia-giordani-irlanda-bergamo-201360552737.shtml|access-date=2021-05-25|website=Corriere della Sera Bergamo|language=it}}</ref> Whilst studying Giordani worked as a chemical health analyst in the Public Health Laboratory of [[Bergamo]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Silvia Giordani|language=English|oclc=4780094036}}</ref> Whilst visiting her uncle in the [[United States]] for a study vacation she was awarded a doctoral scholarship, and eventually ended up a graduate student at the [[University of Miami]].<ref name=":0" /> Her doctoral research considered digital processing at the molecular level. She moved to [[Trinity College Dublin]] for her first postdoctoral research position. Giordani moved to the [[University of Trieste]] for a scientific fellowship.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof Silvia Giordani|url=https://ncsr.ie/people/prof-silvia-giordani/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=National Centre for Sensor Research|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Giordani was awarded the President of Ireland Young Researcher Award to start her independent scientific career at [[Trinity College Dublin]]. She worked as an assistant professor at TCD for six years, before launching her own research laboratory at the [[Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia]]. Her research group considered nano-carbon materials. She moved to the [[University of Turin]] as an associate professor in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mercedes Vasquez - Advanced Processing Technology Centre (APT)|url=https://aptcentre.ie/people/silvia-giordani/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=APT|language=en-US}}</ref> Soon after, she was appointed a full Professor Chair of Nanomaterials within the School of Chemical Sciences at Dublin City University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Researcher Details {{!}}|url=https://www.dcu.ie/researchsupport/research-profile|access-date=2021-05-25|website=Dublin City University|language=en}}</ref> Her research considers nanomaterials and the design of personalised drug delivery systems.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2011-04-04|title=Silvia Giordani, ricercatrice a Dublino coccolata e corteggiata dalla sua Bergamo|url=https://www.bergamonews.it/2011/04/04/silvia-giordani-ricercatrice-a-dublinococcolata-e-corteggiata-dalla-sua-bergamo/144029/|access-date=2021-05-25|website=BergamoNews|language=it-IT}}</ref>
